record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked files were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal-bypass results after a weight edit, testing practical removal but not the original difference-in-means intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports a 32/32 refusal-bypass gate with 0 refusals and 0 garbles. It also mentions 22/22 cyber for the NVIDIA-parent application, but does not define that metric. Listed scripts and work files are not evidence that their code was run.
record.test_reason: A weight edit applied to a newly released model (GLM-5.3-Flash NVFP4) is reported to remove refusals (32/32 bypass, 0 refusals). That is a new-setting result on V2. The edit transplants o_proj weights from an existing abliterated donor rather than computing a difference-in-means direction, so T3 fits better than T2. No unedited baseline is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The README presents the altered Dealign o_proj transplant (L15–43 plus MTP L45, sparing L0–14 and L44) as removing safety refusals on a 32-prompt gate for both parent builds. It says the weights are for research/red-team use only and that users must supply guardrails.
record.recipe_differences: Tool/checkpoint repository. It describes an altered Dealign o_proj transplant on selected layers, not the original difference-in-means direction ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: The README specifies different parent layouts and serving setups; the reported 32/32 gates are associated with raw vLLM/thinking-off for the published weights and Tony DFlash2 for the NVIDIA-parent application.

fits_no_version.finding: The README reports '22/22 cyber' for the NVIDIA-parent build without defining the metric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The edited NVIDIA-parent build scores 22/22 on an unspecified cyber evaluation.

record.problems: The README gives no unedited-parent baseline, uncertainty, or general-capability evaluation. The refusal gate's prompt set and detailed scoring procedure are not stated in the provided text. The cyber result is undefined.
record.rows_left_out: No reported gate results left out. The listed scripts and work files were not treated as results because the repository code was not read or run.

untested.parts: Unedited-parent baseline; general-capability retention (only a garble count is given); prompt sets beyond the 32-prompt gate; models other than GLM-5.3-Flash. The gate is run with thinking off, so behaviour with reasoning on is untested.

missing.what: The README says the MTP L45 o_proj edit was 'required for 32/32' and that residual refusal 'lived late + MTP'. This implies a variant without the MTP edit scored below 32/32, but no number is given. It bears on how the weight edit must be placed to remove refusal.

Editing L44 is described as a garble risk (Dealign Δrel 0.74), and editing early layers as carrying a 'quality tax' learned on another model. These are stated capability costs of the edit, with no measured result in this repo.
missing.locator: README, 'Anchor-safe layer map' and opening table

record.verdict_notes: This is a GitHub tool/checkpoint repo; only the README and file list were available. The work/ folder contains refusal_direction_*.pt files, suggesting direction-based tooling, but the README describes copying donor o_proj weights, so the donor's own method is unstated. The evidence is weak: no baseline, no uncertainty, a small custom gate, and self-reported results.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is identified or ablated; no addition or general-capability test is reported.
The README reports one checkpoint recipe and gate, not broad testing across released models or other refusal evaluations.
No jailbreak-suppression mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of a single direction with affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of training methods or stages.
